brief: Tonight is Legs B — RDL, leg press, curls, extensions, calves and abs. Three lifts go up, because you already beat them on Sunday's leg day and the app was about to hand you last week's numbers anyway. Leg press goes to 180 for both work sets; you finished 160 for 12 and your reps went up during the session, so 160 is done. Leg curl moves to 142.5, because you pulled 135 for 13 twice on Sunday, past the top of the range. Leg extension holds 150 — that one matters, because the app wanted to give you 142.5 tonight, which is lighter than what you already did three days ago. The RDL stays at 205. You rowed heavy yesterday and I am not putting more load on your lower back 24 hours later, so the ask is one extra rep on each top set instead — nine, not eight. If your back starts doing the pulling, stop at eight and it still counts. Calves stay exactly where they were last Legs B, including 260 on the last set: you cut calf work short on Sunday, so finish four honest sets before we add anything. Abs stay at 55 and you beat 13, 12, 12. Cardio is thin — one easy 20 to 30 minute session tomorrow. And about the face pulls: I asked you yesterday to tell me if they felt cooked. You told me. You were right, and the note below says what I want to do about it.

flags.note: You were right about the face pulls. They are in four of your six sessions, which lands them on back-to-back days twice a week, and at 12 sets a week they are tied for the most-trained lift in your whole program. I want to cut them from both push days and keep them only on Pull A and Pull B. Changing the plan is your call, not mine — say yes and I will do it.
About your last calf set: the app's own repeat was going to show you 280 for 15, which you have never done. Last Legs B that set was 260 for 15. Your card tonight shows 260.

Your plank went from 60 seconds to 45 on the last Legs B, both sets, with no note. Your card will still say 60 — I cannot set a timed hold from here. Hold 45, hit it clean twice, and take 60 back next Legs B.
Fourth training day since your last rest day, so you are on day 4 of 6. Nothing to do about it tonight, just know it is coming.

dissent.progression: Hold 205 but ask for 9 reps instead of 8 — he has hit the bottom of the 8-to-10 range on every set, so no weight has been earned yet.
dissent.recovery: Repeat last Legs B exactly at 8 reps — his lower back took four ascending rows to 150x9 yesterday, and a heavy hinge is the only real injury exposure on tonight's card.
dissent.why: Recovery's objection was to added load, and neither seat adds any — the bar sits at 205 either way. One more rep at a weight he has already handled is the honest route to the next 10 pounds and costs the lower back far less than a heavier bar would. I took progression's reps and kept recovery's ceiling on the weight, and I wrote the escape hatch into the brief: if the back starts doing the pulling, eight reps still counts. That is recovery's concern answered without freezing the lift for a third session.

dissent.progression: Push to 280 for all three work sets at 13 reps — 260 is finished, he took it for 15 twice on Sunday.
dissent.recovery: No increase; repeat last Legs B's weights and treat the fourth set as optional, because he voluntarily cut calves to two sets on Sunday.
dissent.why: Progression was asking for a rep record. He has only ever taken 280 for 12, and only twice inside one session — three sets of 13 there would be a number that does not get hit, on a muscle he trimmed himself three days ago. Recovery read that self-cut correctly. Ruling this way also removes the phantom 280x15 the app was going to display, so tonight's card shows the four sets he actually did last Legs B instead of one he has never done.

dissent.progression: Hold 55 and beat 13, 12, 12 — 55 is already proven from Sunday, so there is nothing to progress off yet and no reason to retreat either.
dissent.recovery: Drop back to last Legs B's 50x15 — the trunk is loaded on every leg day and tonight also carries the RDL.
dissent.why: He crunched 55 for 13, 12, 12 three days ago and finished it. Prescribing 50 would put him below his own most recent work, which is exactly the backwards step I am correcting on leg extension tonight, and I will not fix it in one place and commit it in another. Recovery is right that ab volume is high — the program seat found 22 sets a week independently — but the cure for too much ab work is fewer sets in the plan, which is the athlete's call, not a lighter weight tonight.
